imo-isl-2007-a2.prompt:
Consider those functions $f:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ which satisfy the condition
$$f(m+n)\ge f(m)+f\big(f(n)\big)-1$$
for all $m,n\in\mathbb N$. Find all possible values of $f(2007)$.

($\mathbb N$ denotes the set of all positive integers.)
imo-isl-2007-a2.answer: All integers $1,2,\dots,2008$ (one shows $f(n)\le n+1$ for every $n$, and each value is attained).

imo-isl-2007-a3.prompt:
Let $n$ be a positive integer, and let $x$ and $y$ be positive real numbers such that $x^n+y^n=1$. Prove that
$$\left(\sum_{k=1}^n\frac{1+x^{2k}}{1+x^{4k}}\right)\left(\sum_{k=1}^n\frac{1+y^{2k}}{1+y^{4k}}\right)<\frac{1}{(1-x)(1-y)}.$$
imo-isl-2007-a3.answer: For $0<t<1$, $\frac{1+t^2}{1+t^4}<\frac1t$. Summing gives $\sum_k\frac{1+x^{2k}}{1+x^{4k}}<\frac{1-x^n}{x^n(1-x)}=\frac{y^n}{x^n(1-x)}$, and similarly for $y$; multiply.

imo-isl-2007-a4.answer: $f(x)=2x$ (show $f(y)>y$, then $g=f-\mathrm{id}$ is injective, additive and an involution).

imo-isl-2007-a5.prompt:
Let $c>2$, and let $a(1),a(2),\dots$ be a sequence of nonnegative real numbers such that
$$a(m+n)\le 2a(m)+2a(n)\qquad\text{for all } m,n\ge1,$$
and
$$a\big(2^k\big)\le\frac{1}{(k+1)^c}\qquad\text{for all } k\ge0.$$
Prove that the sequence $a(n)$ is bounded.
imo-isl-2007-a5.answer: Weighted subadditivity: if $\sum 2^{-s_i}\le1$ then $a(\sum n_i)\le\sum 2^{s_i}a(n_i)$. Writing $n=\sum 2^{u_i}$ in binary and choosing $2^{s_i}\approx(u_i+1)^{c/2}$ gives $a(n)<4\big(\sum_{m\ge1}m^{-c/2}\big)^2$.

imo-isl-2007-a6.prompt:
Let $a_1,a_2,\dots,a_{100}$ be nonnegative real numbers such that $a_1^2+a_2^2+\dots+a_{100}^2=1$. Prove that
$$a_1^2a_2+a_2^2a_3+\dots+a_{100}^2a_1<\frac{12}{25}.$$
imo-isl-2007-a6.answer: With $S$ the sum, $3S=\sum a_{k+1}\big(a_k^2+2a_{k+1}a_{k+2}\big)$; Cauchy–Schwarz, AM-GM and an odd/even split give $9S^2\le2$, so $S\le\frac{\sqrt2}{3}\approx0.4714<0.48$.

imo-isl-2007-c1.answer: There is exactly one such sequence: $a_{u+vn}=0$ if $u+v\le n$ and $a_{u+vn}=1$ if $u+v\ge n+1$ ($1\le u\le n$, $0\le v\le n$). In blocks of length $n$: $(0\dots0)(0\dots01)(0\dots011)\dots(1\dots1)$, the $v$-th block being $n-v$ zeros followed by $v$ ones.

imo-isl-2007-c2.prompt: A unit square is dissected into $n>1$ rectangles such that their sides are parallel to the sides of the square. Any line, parallel to a side of the square and intersecting its interior, also intersects the interior of some rectangle. Prove that in this dissection, there exists a rectangle having no point on the boundary of the square.
imo-isl-2007-c2.answer: Take a counterexample with the fewest rectangles; no two rectangles share a whole side (else merge them). Looking at the rectangles at the two lower corners and the neighbour of the lower-left one always produces a line that crosses no rectangle — a contradiction.

imo-isl-2007-c3.prompt: Find all positive integers $n$ for which the numbers in the set $S=\{1,2,\dots,n\}$ can be colored red and blue, with the following condition being satisfied: the set $S\times S\times S$ contains exactly $2007$ ordered triples $(x,y,z)$ such that (i) $x,y,z$ are of the same color and (ii) $x+y+z$ is divisible by $n$.

imo-isl-2007-c4.prompt:
Let $A_0=(a_1,\dots,a_n)$ be a finite sequence of real numbers. For each $k\ge0$, from the sequence $A_k=(x_1,\dots,x_n)$ we construct a new sequence $A_{k+1}$ in the following way.

1. We choose a partition $\{1,\dots,n\}=I\cup J$, where $I$ and $J$ are two disjoint sets, such that the expression
$$\Big|\sum_{i\in I}x_i-\sum_{j\in J}x_j\Big|$$
attains the smallest possible value. (We allow the sets $I$ or $J$ to be empty; in this case the corresponding sum is $0$.) If there are several such partitions, one is chosen arbitrarily.

2. We set $A_{k+1}=(y_1,\dots,y_n)$, where $y_i=x_i+1$ if $i\in I$, and $y_i=x_i-1$ if $i\in J$.

Prove that for some $k$, the sequence $A_k$ contains an element $x$ such that $|x|\ge n/2$.
imo-isl-2007-c4.answer: If all $|x_i|<a$ there is a partition with $\big|\sum_I-\sum_J\big|<a$. So if every entry always stayed in $(-n/2,n/2)$, the sum of squares would strictly increase at each step, impossible because only finitely many sequences can occur.

imo-isl-2007-c5.prompt: In the Cartesian coordinate plane define the strip $S_n=\{(x,y)\mid n\le x<n+1\}$ for every integer $n$. Assume that each strip $S_n$ is colored either red or blue, and let $a$ and $b$ be two distinct positive integers. Prove that there exists a rectangle with side lengths $a$ and $b$ such that its vertices have the same color.
imo-isl-2007-c5.answer: If $S_n,S_{n+a}$ or $S_n,S_{n+b}$ ever share a colour, use an axis-parallel rectangle. Otherwise, with $d=\gcd(a,b)$, strips $d$ apart always differ (so the colouring has period $2d$); a tilted rectangle whose side $a$ has horizontal projection $2d$ and an irrational offset for the other pair of vertices can then be placed with all four vertices in one colour.

imo-isl-2007-c7.prompt: Let $\alpha<\frac{3-\sqrt5}{2}$ be a positive real number. Prove that there exist positive integers $n$ and $p>\alpha\cdot2^n$ for which one can select $2p$ pairwise distinct subsets $S_1,\dots,S_p,T_1,\dots,T_p$ of the set $\{1,2,\dots,n\}$ such that $S_i\cap T_j\ne\varnothing$ for all $1\le i,j\le p$.
imo-isl-2007-c7.answer: Split $\{1,\dots,km\}$ into $k$ blocks of size $m$. Let $\mathcal S$ be the sets meeting every block and $\mathcal T$ the sets that contain a whole block but are not in $\mathcal S$. With $k\approx2^m\ln\frac1\delta$, both families have density tending to $\delta=\frac{3-\sqrt5}{2}$ (because $1-2\delta+\delta^2=\delta$).

imo-isl-2007-c8.prompt:
Given a convex $n$-gon $P$ in the plane. For every three vertices of $P$, consider the triangle determined by them. Call such a triangle *good* if all its sides are of unit length.

Prove that there are not more than $\frac23n$ good triangles.
imo-isl-2007-c8.answer: Each vertex $A$ "assigns" at most two good triangles: those through the two extreme partner points on the unit circle around $A$. Every good triangle receives at least three assignments, so $3t\le2n$.

imo-isl-2007-g2.prompt:
Given an isosceles triangle $ABC$ with $AB=AC$. The midpoint of side $BC$ is denoted by $M$. Let $X$ be a variable point on the shorter arc $MA$ of the circumcircle of triangle $ABM$. Let $T$ be the point in the angle domain $BMA$, for which $\angle TMX=90^\circ$ and $TX=BX$.

Prove that $\angle MTB-\angle CTM$ does not depend on $X$.
imo-isl-2007-g2.answer: It always equals $\angle MAB$. With $N$ the midpoint of $BT$: $MN\parallel CT$ and $M,N$ lie on the circle with diameter $XT$, so $\angle MTB=\angle MXN$ and $\angle CTM=\angle NXT=\angle BXN$; the difference is $\angle MXB=\angle MAB$.

imo-isl-2007-g3.prompt: The diagonals of a trapezoid $ABCD$ intersect at point $P$. Point $Q$ lies between the parallel lines $BC$ and $AD$ such that $\angle AQD=\angle CQB$, and line $CD$ separates points $P$ and $Q$. Prove that $\angle BQP=\angle DAQ$.
imo-isl-2007-g3.answer: The homothety $h$ with centre $P$ and ratio $-\frac{AD}{BC}$ maps $B\mapsto D$, $C\mapsto A$, $Q\mapsto Q'$. Then $\angle AQ'D=\angle CQB=\angle AQD$, so $AQ'QD$ is cyclic, and $\angle DAQ=\angle DQ'Q=\angle DQ'P=\angle BQP$.

imo-isl-2007-g5.prompt: Let $ABC$ be a fixed triangle, and let $A_1,B_1,C_1$ be the midpoints of sides $BC,CA,AB$, respectively. Let $P$ be a variable point on the circumcircle. Let lines $PA_1,PB_1,PC_1$ meet the circumcircle again at $A',B',C'$, respectively. Assume that the points $A,B,C,A',B',C'$ are distinct, and lines $AA',BB',CC'$ form a triangle. Prove that the area of this triangle does not depend on $P$.
imo-isl-2007-g5.answer: The area is always $\frac12[ABC]$. By Pascal's theorem the vertices of the triangle lie on the midlines of $ABC$. Parallel midlines then give $A_0C_0\cdot B_0C_0=AC_0\cdot BC_0$, so the area equals $[ABC_0]=\frac12[ABC]$.

imo-isl-2007-g6.prompt:
Determine the smallest positive real number $k$ with the following property.

Let $ABCD$ be a convex quadrilateral, and let points $A_1$, $B_1$, $C_1$ and $D_1$ lie on sides $AB$, $BC$, $CD$ and $DA$, respectively. Consider the areas of triangles $AA_1D_1$, $BB_1A_1$, $CC_1B_1$, and $DD_1C_1$; let $S$ be the sum of the two smallest ones, and let $S_1$ be the area of quadrilateral $A_1B_1C_1D_1$. Then we always have $kS_1\ge S$.

imo-isl-2007-g7.prompt:
Given an acute triangle $ABC$ with angles $\alpha$, $\beta$ and $\gamma$ at vertices $A$, $B$ and $C$, respectively, such that $\beta>\gamma$. Point $I$ is the incenter, and $R$ is the circumradius. Point $D$ is the foot of the altitude from vertex $A$. Point $K$ lies on line $AD$ such that $AK=2R$, and $D$ separates $A$ and $K$. Finally, lines $DI$ and $KI$ meet sides $AC$ and $BC$ at $E$ and $F$, respectively.

Prove that if $IE=IF$ then $\beta\le3\gamma$.
imo-isl-2007-g7.answer: Key fact: $\angle KID=\frac{\beta-\gamma}{2}$ always. If $IE=IF$, the right triangles $IEB_1$ and $IFA_1$ are congruent, so $CEIF$ is either cyclic (giving $\gamma=\frac{\beta-\gamma}2$, i.e. $\beta=3\gamma$) or a kite with acute angles at $E$ and $F$ (giving $\gamma>\frac{\beta-\gamma}{2}$).

imo-isl-2007-g8.prompt: Point $P$ lies on side $AB$ of a convex quadrilateral $ABCD$. Let $\omega$ be the incircle of triangle $CPD$, and let $I$ be its incenter. Suppose that $\omega$ is tangent to the incircles of triangles $APD$ and $BPC$ at points $K$ and $L$, respectively. Let lines $AC$ and $BD$ meet at $E$, and let lines $AK$ and $BL$ meet at $F$. Prove that points $E$, $I$, and $F$ are collinear.
imo-isl-2007-g8.answer: Let $\Omega$ be the circle tangent to segment $AB$ and rays $AD$, $BC$, with centre $J$. By the three-homothety (Monge) theorem, $F$ is the centre of the negative homothety and $E$ the centre of the positive homothety taking $\omega$ to $\Omega$. So both lie on the line $IJ$.

imo-isl-2007-n1.prompt: Find all pairs $(k,n)$ of positive integers for which $7^k-3^n$ divides $k^4+n^2$.

imo-isl-2007-n2.prompt: Let $b,n>1$ be integers. Suppose that for each $k>1$ there exists an integer $a_k$ such that $b-a_k^n$ is divisible by $k$. Prove that $b=A^n$ for some integer $A$.
imo-isl-2007-n2.answer: Use $k=b^2$. For each prime $p^\alpha\,\|\,b$, we get $a^n\equiv b\pmod{p^{\alpha+1}}$, so $p^\alpha\,\|\,a^n$ and $n\mid\alpha$.

imo-isl-2007-n3.prompt: Let $X$ be a set of $10\,000$ integers, none of them divisible by $47$. Prove that there exists a $2007$-element subset $Y$ of $X$ such that $a-b+c-d+e$ is not divisible by $47$ for any $a,b,c,d,e\in Y$.
imo-isl-2007-n3.answer: $J=\{\pm1,\pm3,\pm5,\pm7,\pm9\}$ is "good" ($a-b+c-d+e$ is odd with absolute value $\le45$). Each $x\in X$ satisfies $kx\bmod47\in J$ for exactly $10$ values $k\in\{1,\dots,46\}$, so some $k$ works for at least $\frac{100\,000}{46}>2007$ elements.

imo-isl-2007-n4.prompt:
For every integer $k\ge2$, prove that $2^{3k}$ divides the number
$$\binom{2^{k+1}}{2^k}-\binom{2^k}{2^{k-1}}$$
but $2^{3k+1}$ does not.
imo-isl-2007-n4.answer: The difference equals $\frac{2^{2^k}(2^k-1)!!}{(2^k)!}\cdot P(2^k)$, where $P(x)=\prod_{i}(x+2i-1)-\prod_i(x-2i+1)$ (product over $i=1,\dots,2^{k-1}$). The first factor has $2$-adic valuation $1$. $P$ is odd, $P(x)=x^3Q(x)+cx$, and $v_2(c)=2k-1$, so $v_2\big(P(2^k)\big)=3k-1$.

imo-isl-2007-n5.prompt:
Find all surjective functions $f:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ such that for every $m,n\in\mathbb N$ and every prime $p$, the number $f(m+n)$ is divisible by $p$ if and only if $f(m)+f(n)$ is divisible by $p$.

($\mathbb N$ is the set of all positive integers.)
imo-isl-2007-n5.answer: $f(n)=n$ (show that $f$ preserves residues modulo every prime $p$ and that $p\mid f(x)\iff p\mid x$; then induct).

imo-isl-2007-n6.prompt: Let $k$ be a positive integer. Prove that the number $(4k^2-1)^2$ has a positive divisor of the form $8kn-1$ if and only if $k$ is even.
imo-isl-2007-n6.answer: Lemma (this is IMO 2007 Problem 5): $4xy-1\mid(4x^2-1)^2$ only when $x=y$, proved by infinite descent. Apply it with $x=k$, $y=2n$: such a divisor exists exactly when $k=2n$.

imo-isl-2007-n7.prompt: For a prime $p$ and a positive integer $n$, denote by $\nu_p(n)$ the exponent of $p$ in the prime factorization of $n!$. Given a positive integer $d$ and a finite set $\{p_1,\dots,p_k\}$ of primes. Show that there are infinitely many positive integers $n$ such that $d\mid\nu_{p_i}(n)$ for all $1\le i\le k$.
imo-isl-2007-n7.answer:
If $p^K\mid N$ and $0<r<p^K$, then $
u_p(N+r)=
u_p(N)+
u_p(r)$. So $
u_{p_i}$ is additive on sums of terms of the fast-growing sequence $n_1=1$, $n_{\ell+1}=(p_1\cdots p_k)^{n_\ell}$. By pigeonhole, infinitely many terms have the same residues mod $d$, and any $d$ of them sum to a valid $n$.
